parts.note: to back someone is to support them
something brought down has been reduced, as prices are marked down

explanation.surface: A team whose backing has dwindled has little option but to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is the idiom for retreating from a position or yielding in an argument.

clue.text: Fail to include note in part of Bible

indicators.note: the note is placed in the middle of the Bible section, splitting it

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament
MI is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A reader complains that a musical note was left out of a Bible passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to leave something out is to fail to include it.

clue.text: Danger could come from this plot

indicators.note: the clue says the word Danger could be made from the answer's letters, so the two are rearrangements of each other

explanation.surface: A warning that some patch of land hides a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: rearranging the answer gives 'Danger', so rearranging 'Danger' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small area of ground, such as a vegetable or flower patch.

parts.note: a pub landlord is the host who receives guests

explanation.surface: Praise for a publican who is in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spirit' reads as a mood, but 'in' is only a link and 'spirit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit of the dead seen by the living is a phantom or spectre.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words baggy moleskins, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: Someone working out while wearing loose moleskin trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for gymnastics, a term for physical exercises, as in a school PE lesson.

parts.note: BOD is slang for a person, as in 'an odd bod'
ICE is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone with jewels tucked in a waistcoat pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting upper garment, a sleeveless vest or waistcoat worn over a blouse or shift.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south or southern
a sign is a written symbol or character

explanation.surface: Describing a conference delegate as a character from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it over or allot it to someone else.

clue.text: Accelerate when favourite's back in the lead

indicators.note: back means the word for favourite's is read from right to left

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, so favourite's gives PET plus S
a competitor in front is up on the rest

explanation.surface: A racing tip: push on when the favoured horse returns to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of favourite's supplies the S of PETS before 'back' turns it round.

clue.text: Companion, male not female, is soft

parts.note: a fellow is a comrade or companion

explanation.surface: Describing a gentle-natured partner who is a man rather than a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Of colours, sounds or flavours: gentle and smooth rather than harsh.

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Asking how old an English painter is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a long historical period, such as the Victorian epoch.

clue.text: Minister, one in front of Vatican vehicle

indicators.note: the numeral for one is placed before the word for vehicle

parts.note: V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City
I is the Roman numeral for one
a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A clergyman parked ahead of the Pope's car.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England is a minister of religion.

parts.note: IN means fashionable or popular
having a hand in something is having agency or involvement in it

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a matter being dealt with and managed is said to be well looked after.

definitions.meaning: a sum of money paid as punishment for an offence

parts.note: something accomplished is finished or over
the cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A review: skilled performers, yet a tedious show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' suggests skilful, but it means completed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Said of the sky or weather: cloudy and grey, gloomy rather than bright.

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down
ABOUT means concerning, as does on: a book on or about birds

explanation.surface: Seems to tell someone to place something on a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loafer' suggests a slip-on shoe, but it is an idle person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an idler who avoids work and lounges about.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a kid is a child; the apostrophe-S is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A toddler's playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle or foot losing grip and sliding sideways is said to skate uncontrollably.

clue.text: Surge forward, grasping nothing, and sprawl

indicators.note: the word for a surge forward holds the letter for nothing within its grip

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden forward thrust
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone rushes ahead, clutches at air, and ends up flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll or recline lazily, stretched out on a sofa.

clue.text: Meaning heartless and confused: a puzzle

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
heartless asks for the central letter of the word Meaning to be removed

explanation.surface: Something whose sense is muddled and missing its core is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle N of MEANING, leaving MEAING, which 'confused' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery or riddle, something hard to understand, is a puzzle.

indicators.note: the word for reduction is put in the middle of the word for fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
a loss is a reduction or decrease

explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: enormous, gigantic, of great size.

clue.text: Vast sum of money for herb

definitions.meaning: a fortune, as in 'it cost a ...'
an aromatic garden plant used in cooking and sauces

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for a fortune and is also the name of a common culinary plant.

parts.note: something good is pleasant or enjoyable
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A tourist's delighted exclamation at a pleasant trip to a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!' or 'Goodness me!'.

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for school

parts.note: a pod is a school or group of whales or dolphins

parts.note: ire is anger or wrath

explanation.surface: Temper flares in a school during term time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests education, but here it is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of time, such as an academic term or session.

clue.text: Chaps coming round to help young unmarried girl

indicators.note: the word for chaps encircles the word for help

parts.note: chaps are men
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Young men arriving to assist a single girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or literary word for a girl or young woman not yet married.

indicators.note: horrid suggests something mangled or messed up, so the word lie is rearranged

explanation.surface: An urge to cover up an awful falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To veil something is to cover or hide it from view.

definitions.meaning: a white wine from the Rhineland
informal British slang for to pawn
